topicName: Asynchronous Processing & Long-Running Operations (Webhooks, Polling, 202 Accepted)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Asynchronous Processing & Long-Running Operations in REST APIs"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"When designing RESTful APIs, certain operations cannot be completed within a standard HTTP request-response lifecycle. Heavy computations, large file processing, or third-party integrations can cause gateway timeouts. To maintain a responsive system, developers use asynchronous processing patterns."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The 202 Accepted Status Code"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"The HTTP 202 Accepted status code indicates that the request has been received for processing, but the processing has not been completed. It is non-committal, meaning there is no guarantee that the operation will eventually succeed. The response body should typically include a resource location or a task identifier for status tracking."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
Content-Type: application/json
Location: https://api.example.com/v1/tasks/9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d

{
  "taskId": "9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d",
  "status": "processing",
  "statusUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1/tasks/9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d"
}"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"Pattern 1: Polling"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Polling involves the client periodically sending GET requests to the status endpoint provided in the initial 202 response until the operation completes. While simple to implement, polling can introduce unnecessary network traffic and server load if not designed properly."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use exponential backoff to reduce the frequency of status check requests over time."},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always implement a maximum retry limit or timeout to prevent infinite loops."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"GET /v1/tasks/9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "taskId": "9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d",
  "status": "completed",
  "resultUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1/reports/final-report.pdf"
}"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Pattern 2: Webhooks (Callbacks)"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Webhooks provide an event-driven alternative to polling. Instead of the client asking for updates, the server sends an HTTP POST request to a pre-registered client URL (callback URL) once the long-running operation finishes."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The client registers a webhook URL during the initial request payload."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"The server securely delivers the payload upon task completion, utilizing cryptographic signatures to verify authenticity."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"POST /webhook-receiver HTTP/1.1
Host: client.example.com
Content-Type: application/json
X-Signature: sha256=abcdef123456...

{
  "event": "task.completed",
  "taskId": "9b1deb4d-3b7d-4bad-9bdd-2b0d7b3dcb6d",
  "status": "success",
  "data": {
    "downloadUrl": "https://api.example.com/v1/reports/final-report.pdf"
  }
}"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Implementation"},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Idempotency: Ensure that retried requests or duplicate webhook deliveries do not trigger duplicate processing."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Security: Always use HTTPS for webhook endpoints and validate request signatures (HMAC) to prevent spoofing."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Resource Cleanup: Establish a retention policy to purge completed task states and temporary files after a specific time frame."}]
